questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Tool Selection Matrix?
choices: To list all available AI tools in alphabetical order
To compare tools using weighted criteria so you can choose the best fit for a specific task
To track how much each tool costs per month
To replace the need for testing tools before use
questions.explanation: A Tool Selection Matrix provides a structured comparison using weighted criteria and a scoring system, helping you select the most appropriate tool for a given task based on your priorities.

questions.question: Why should you assign weights to criteria in a Tool Selection Matrix rather than treating all criteria equally?
choices: Weights make the matrix look more professional in presentations
Different criteria have different importance depending on your project's context and priorities
Weights are required by the AI tool API specification
Equal criteria always produce incorrect results
questions.explanation: Not all criteria matter equally for every project. Weighting allows you to prioritize factors like accuracy, speed, cost, or ease-of-use based on what matters most for your specific use case.

questions.question: What is a common mistake when building a Tool Selection Matrix?
choices: Including too many criteria and making the comparison overly complex
Using only one tool in the comparison
Always choosing the highest-scoring tool without considering trade-offs
Both A and C are common mistakes
questions.explanation: Overcomplicating the matrix with too many criteria makes it unwieldy, and blindly picking the top scorer ignores important trade-offs. A good matrix balances comprehensiveness with practicality.
